requirements.evidence: Contract and main rules are present: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:16 `__invoke(Queue $queue, User $calledBy, CallMode $mode = CallMode::Any): Ticket`; queue row locked and re-read (:20-27); deterministic ordering (:113-117 `orderByDesc('priority')->orderBy('issued_at')->orderBy('id')`); fairness history (:76-91, last 3 called by `called_at`/`id`); exactly-once lock-and-recheck loop (:42-71); InactiveQueueException (:26) and NoWaitingTicketsException (:46); both docs updated (docs/architecture.md:119-134, docs/business-rules.md:100-101 and :117-120). Gap: the fairness restriction is decided once at :29-37 and a raced normal at :61-63 ends in NoWaitingTicketsException instead of the task's fallback to priority tickets (task.md:34-35).

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an invokable action (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:14-15) matching conventions.md:42-45; Eloquent setter writes avoid mass assignment (:66-69); docs kept in sync for the two docs the task names (docs/architecture.md:119-134, docs/business-rules.md:117-120). Deviation: CHANGELOG.md is not touched although conventions.md:103 asks for an `[Unreleased]` entry; no test files (see tests).

security.evidence: Task explicitly waives authorization (task.md:11-12) and no untrusted input enters the action; mode is a backed enum, queue/user are models. Only the write-once-allowed fields are set (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:66-69) so the model guard holds; no raw output, no secrets, no mass-assignment surface. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: change.diff declares only app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, app/Enums/CallMode.php, app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php and two docs; there is no test file at all, so fairness, the three modes, inactive-queue rejection and the exactly-once race are unverified (conventions.md:12-21).

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: one action, reuse of Ticket/Queue, no new layers (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:14-74). Some duplication: `nextCandidate` (:97-121) and `matchesMode` (:123-134) repeat the same mode/priority filtering, and the `restrictToNormal` flag is threaded through both.

readability.evidence: Small focused private methods with clear names (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:76 `hasPriorityStreak`, :97 `nextCandidate`, :123 `matchesMode`); comments explain the locking intent (:49-51). Minor unevenness: `$ticket->priority > 0` at :126 versus `$ticket->priority === 0` at :130, and the carried boolean flag.

scope.evidence: Diff touches only the action, its enum, its exception and the two docs the task requires (change.diff:1-261); no unrelated refactors, UI, authorization or Livewire work.

issues.explanation: The change ships zero Pest/PHPUnit tests for a concurrency-critical domain action, breaking the project's mandatory test-first rule (conventions.md:12-21) and leaving fairness, mode selection, exception paths and the exactly-once race completely unverified.

The fairness restriction is computed once before the loop; if the only waiting normal is called concurrently and skipped at :61-63, the next iteration finds no candidate and throws NoWaitingTicketsException, whereas task.md:34-35 says priority tickets must keep being called when no normal is waiting.

`matchesMode` uses strict `$ticket->priority === 0` while every other check uses `> 0`; if the attribute is returned as a string (uncast model/certain drivers) every normal candidate fails the re-check, is skipped, and the call ends in a spurious NoWaitingTicketsException.
`firstOrFail()` on the candidate row turns a concurrently deleted ticket into ModelNotFoundException rather than the required 'skip and pick the next one' behaviour.
conventions.md:103 requires an `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry when behaviour changes, and the new call-next action is not recorded.

Mode/priority filtering is expressed twice (SQL in `nextCandidate`, PHP in `matchesMode`) with a `restrictToNormal` flag passed through both; a single candidate predicate would be easier to keep consistent.
`return $locked->refresh();` issues an extra SELECT; `$locked` already holds the saved values, so the refresh adds a query without changing the result.

review.summary: Adds the CallNextTicket action with the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException and the required architecture/business-rules docs, implementing mode selection, ordering, the 3-call fairness rule and a lock-based exactly-once loop. The implementation is close to the contract and well structured, but it ships no tests at all, which the project treats as non-negotiable, and the fairness fallback fails when the last waiting normal is lost to a race.
